test_intent: Verifies that NotificationService.SendSuspiciousMessageWithButtons sends a notification message when the suspicious message text is 1000 characters long.
reason: The assertion only verifies SendMessage was called once with It.IsAny for all parameters, providing no content validation. Long text handling is an implementation detail of the notification template layer, not a distinct bot contract. The same behavior is already covered by the general happy-path test (SendSuspiciousMessageWithButtons_WithValidData_SendsMessageWithButtons). The test also reads message.MessageId which is unreliable in test construction. No replacement needed because there is no distinct production contract for long-text handling beyond the general notification path.

test_intent: Verifies that NotificationService.SendSuspiciousMessageWithButtons sends a notification when the message text contains markdown formatting characters and emoji.
reason: Identical structure to the long-text variant: only verifies SendMessage was called once with It.IsAny for all parameters. Does not verify that special characters are properly escaped or handled. The test reads message.MessageId (unreliable in test construction). No distinct bot contract exists for special-character handling in notifications beyond the general happy path. If escaping correctness matters, it should be tested at the MessageTemplates seam with state assertions on the generated string, not via mock verification at the notification service level.

test_intent: Verifies that calling MessageHandler.HandleCommandAsync with a /stats command does not throw an exception.
reason: Assert.DoesNotThrowAsync without any outcome assertion is a strong delete signal per audit guidance. It provides zero behavioral coverage beyond compile-time smoke. The actual routing behavior (that the command reaches CommandRouter) is already tested by the mock_verify tests in the same class. No replacement needed because the routing contract is covered elsewhere.

test_intent: Verifies that MessageHandler.HandleCommandAsync delegates a /stats command to CommandRouter.HandleCommandAsync.
reason: Tests the core MessageHandler routing contract: commands are forwarded to CommandRouter. The mock_verify assertion on CommandRouter.HandleCommandAsync is a meaningful behavioral check. Uses legacy_message_handler_test_factory which adds maintenance overhead, but the test is small, focused, and covers a real bot contract. The routing seam is correct for this behavior.

test_intent: Claims to verify command routing with empty stats data, but uses the same TK.CreateStatsCommandMessage() as other tests with no actual variation.
reason: Exact duplicate of HandleCommandAsync_WithCustomStats_RoutesThroughCommandRouter: same Arrange (TK.CreateStatsCommandMessage, CommandRouter returns true), same Act, same Verify. The name suggests empty-stats edge case but the implementation is identical. No distinct behavior is tested. No replacement needed because the routing contract is already covered by the non-duplicate test.

test_intent: Verifies that MessageHandler.HandleCommandAsync calls CommandRouter even when the router returns false (command not handled).
reason: Tests a distinct behavioral variant from the happy-path test: CommandRouter is called regardless of its return value. The mock setup returns false (vs true in other tests), confirming the handler does not short-circuit before calling the router. This is a meaningful routing contract. Small, focused, correct seam.
